 Show Most recent Most popular It feels like 'open season' for Man Utd published at 22:33 BST 22:33 BST 
 FT: Como 4-1 Manchester United 
 Matt Upson 
Former Arsenal defender on BBC Radio 5 Live 
 What teams aren't in better shape and form than Manchester United? Manchester United for me get results because they spent a lot of money and they do have players that can do things, and they will win some football matches, but at the moment it's just open season it feels at the club.
 That's a very difficult thing to deal with, can you be successful on the pitch when that's going on? Probably not, I don't think that's possible. I wasn't surprised to see that they really struggled against a team that's on the complete opposite side of where they are. 
 [Como are] together, fresh, new, have something to prove and grabbing their opportunity as a group. 
 There is something definitely wrong, and to criticise not the manager directly, but the tactics, which land at his feet is so damaging.

 'A fascinating game' published at 22:31 BST 22:31 BST 
 FT: Bayern Munich 2-2 Arsenal 
 Arsenal 
 Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta, speaking to TNT Sports: "That is one of the highest levels we played. Two teams who wanted to press each other and wanted to attack and wanted to play. It was a fascinating game. 
 "We started the game incredibly well, we were so dominant. Then we had to adapt without Saka. In the second half the game was a bit even and they scored the goals and we had to react, which we did. We scored and we had the chance to win it too. That is the level."
 On Saka's injury: "They are a bit concerned. A player who has to come off with a really sharp pain is never good news but we have to wait and see."

 'Kane is the clear winner of Ballon d'or' published at 22:20 BST 22:20 BST 
 FT: Bayern Munich 2-2 Arsenal 
 Bayern Munich 
 Arsenal midfielder Declan Rice, speaking to TNT Sports about Harry Kane for Ballon d'Or: "He is the clear winner. His numbers speak for themselves, the year he has had has been remarkable. When you play with him you realise how good he is and when you play against him you see how much of a pain it is.
 "He is ridiculous, such a good player and I am lucky I can play with him, not so lucky I have to play against him."
 On his goal: "When you play against teams who are man to man all over the pitch you have to apply certain principles. They follow you all over the pitch but I lost my man and I just kept running and lot my runner and then I was in on the goal. So happy. Gyokeres has been making such a good impact coming off the bench. He made some great runs tonight and set me up for the goal.
 "It is what the manager has drilled into us. We aren't just going to come here and sit. At home they are probably one of the best teams in Europe so to come here tonight and give that account of ourselves was really good. We have to keep going."

 By Phil McNulty Chief football writer at Villa Park Aston Villa continued the impressive start to their Champions League campaign with a comfortable victory over Viking at Villa Park. 
 Villa made it three wins from three, following their 6-0 demolition of Fenerbahce, by easing past the Norwegian side who pushed Bayern Munich all the way to draw 3-3 in the last round of matches.
 Unai Emery's side were on top from the start, Viking living dangerously on several occasions before Ross Barkley turned in Ibrahim Mbaye's corner at the near post after 23 minutes.
 Villa continued to dominate and doubled their lead eight minutes before half-time, Emiliano Buendia scoring from the spot after Alysson was tripped by Zlatko Tripic, the decision given after a Video Assistant Referee (VAR) review.
 Viking showed more attacking intent at the start of the second half, but Villa wrapped up another three points in the Champions League when the impressive Alysson's cross was turned into his own net by Henrik Heggheim after 62 minutes.
 It paved the way for a comfortable conclusion as Villa closed out a victory that was another emphatic statement from the great European specialist Emery.
 Alejandro Garnacho, who has struggled to make an impact at Villa since his loan move from Chelsea, emerged as a substitute to produce a lively cameo, almost getting on the scoresheet, only to see his shot saved by Viking keeper Arlid Ostbo.
 Viking pulled a goal back with four minutes left, Peter Christiansen's acrobatic finish given by VAR after initially being ruled offside, but nothing could spoil another satisfying night for Emery, Villa's 12th consecutive home win in European competition.
 How Aston Villa's players rated 
 Zion Suzuki: Not a huge amount to do, but what he did was done with confidence. Will have been disappointed to miss out on a clean sheet late on. 6 
 Victor Lindelof: Couple of decent clearances but hardly under any stress all night. 6 
 Tyrone Mings: Comfortable night as Villa dominated apart from brief Viking threats. 6 
 Pau Torres: Calm and composed at the back. Rarely troubled. 6 
 Ross Barkley: Clever near post header for Villa's opener and enjoyed the space he was given in midfield to show his creative side. 7 
 John McGinn: Typical "Super John McGinn" performance. At the heart of everything. Tackling. Passing. Just what Villa fans have come to love. 7 
 Alysson: Lively and dangerous out wide. Won the penalty for Emiliano Buendia to score and set up other dangerous opportunities. Real pace and deserved a goal for his efforts. 8 
 Ibrahim Mbaye : Sent in the perfect delivery from a corner for Barkley's opener and was always energetic. 6 
 Joao Gomes: Took a knock early but recovered. Solid in the midfield base, ambitious with his passing and saw a cross deflected on to the bar. 7 
 Emilianio Buendia: Creator. Should have scored with a first half header but coolly slotted home his penalty. 7 
 Nicolas Jackson: Often a threat but not on target this time. Should have scored with two early headers. 6 
 Substitutes: 
 Tammy Abraham (on 70, Jackson): No time to make a serious impact. 5 
 Leon Goretzka (on 70, Barkley): Brought on to secure the win with his experience. 6 
 Matty Cash (on 71, Joao Gomes): Barely anything to do. 5 
 Alejandro Garnacho (on 72, Mbiaye): Lively cameo. Could have had a goal. Might boost fragile confidence. 6 
 George Hemmings (on 75, Alysson): 
 Subs not used: 
 Bizot, Wright, Harwood-Bellis, Kamara, Maatsen, Bogarde.
